quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: The posted speed limit.
A speed that is faster than reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must not drive faster than is reasonable and safe. Adjust your speed based on the road, traffic, weather, pedestrians, and light. You must also stay within the posted speed limit.

questions.question: Which is NOT a factor in how far it takes to stop your vehicle?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on speed and road conditions.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph may need up to ____ feet to stop completely.

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Large trucks take much longer to stop than cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer may need about 400 feet to stop when traveling at 55 mph.

questions.question: When you see a steady green arrow on a traffic signal, you:

options.text: Must merge into the lane pointing in the direction of the arrow.
Should slow down and stop if it is safe.
May turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection pass.
May drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: May turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection pass.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane for the turn. Always yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

questions.question: When entering the highway on a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Immediately move to the right lane and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder to speed up to match traffic.
Speed up only after you see a gap in traffic, then enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you see a gap in traffic, then enter.
questions.explanation: On a short entrance ramp without an acceleration lane, wait for a gap in traffic. Speed up and enter only when you can do so safely.

questions.question: It is legal to drive faster than the speed limit when passing another vehicle.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You cannot drive faster than the posted speed limit at any time, including when passing other vehicles.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Turn the wheel too far in the other direction.
Turn your wheel toward traffic.
Turn your wheel in the direction the vehicle is skidding.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheel in the direction the vehicle is skidding.
questions.explanation: Stay calm if your vehicle skids. Steer in the direction the back of the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: A solid white line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same way. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Signal as you move into the new lane.
Signal 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.
Always check your blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Cars and motorcycles can be hidden in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet ahead on residential streets or 5 seconds before on freeways.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No left turn is allowed here.
You can turn left only after stopping.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn is allowed here.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign prohibits left turns.

questions.question: What are regulatory signs?

options.text: They are placed everywhere there is danger.
They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
They warn drivers about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black markings on white. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. They show speed limits, no passing signs, or other driving rules.

questions.question: When you get in a car to drive, what should you adjust first?

options.text: Your seat belt
The steering wheel
Your rearview mirror
Your seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat first so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel based on your seat position.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should you turn?

options.text: Into any lane
Into the first lane
Into the second lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Into the first lane
questions.explanation: Always turn from your lane into the first available legal lane. When turning onto a one-way street, turn into the first lane.

questions.question: When exiting the interstate, when should you slow down?

options.text: About halfway through the deceleration lane
As you approach the deceleration lane
Right when you enter the deceleration lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane
questions.explanation: Keep your speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator sticks open while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn
Slam on your brakes
Turn on your four-way flashers
Turn off your ignition carefully so the steering wheel doesn't lock

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition carefully so the steering wheel doesn't lock
questions.explanation: A stuck accelerator means your car will keep going fast even if you lift your foot. Turn off the ignition by moving the switch just enough to stop the engine without locking the wheel. Then apply your brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Road construction ahead
The road curves left then right
The road curves right then left

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right then left
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers the road ahead will curve right, then curve left. Slow down and be ready for these curves.

questions.question: You come to an intersection blocked by other traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Go slowly until traffic ahead moves
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through it
Sound your horn to make cars move up

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through it
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if you cannot get all the way through. Wait for traffic ahead to clear so you don't block the intersection.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what should you usually do?

options.text: Go slowly while waiting for an opening
Speed up faster than freeway traffic
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway
Speed up to match freeway traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match freeway traffic
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic so you can blend in safely. You must yield to cars already on the freeway.

questions.question: At an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should you stop?

options.text: You do not have to stop
Slow down to check if crossing traffic is clear
Stop where you can see at least 200 feet on either side, even if you enter the intersecting roadway
Stop where you can see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway
questions.explanation: Stop at the closest safe spot to the intersecting roadway where you can see traffic coming. Do not enter the intersecting roadway to get a better view.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed with caution
Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming
questions.explanation: At these locations, look left and right to check if anyone is crossing or entering your path.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, what should you do?

options.text: Stop right away and let the vehicle pass.
Move safely to the right side of the road and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep driving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move safely to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses lights and/or a siren, move your car as far right as you can safely go and stop. Do not stop inside an intersection. This applies no matter which direction the emergency vehicle is coming from.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if other cars are coming.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Go through the intersection carefully without always stopping.
Stop only if there is traffic on the crossing road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must stop completely. Let other vehicles and pedestrians pass. Then go when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A driver ahead does not dim their high beam headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the other vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight ahead down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the bright lights. You can still see the road and stay in your lane until the other car passes.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?

options.text: Start to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Honk your horn loudly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn loudly.
questions.explanation: Use a loud horn blast when a child or pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your moving car. This warns them of danger.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Use light braking.
Do not use the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, do not brake. Braking can make the skid worse.
